entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:1
segments: There is an evil; the Preacher has shown that the power to enjoy good aright is the gift of God, and is the sum of earthly blessings.

He now considers the opposite case. 
 
It is easy for God to imbitter to men all their earthly possessions, so that while they are surrounded by wealth their souls shall be in the deepest poverty.  The true enjoyment of life lies not in the abundance of outward good, but rather in a cheerful and contented spirit; especially in a humble resignation of ourselves to his all-powerful disposal, with unwavering faith in him for the present and the future.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:2
segments:
Giveth him not power to eat thereof; either through the influence of tormenting passions, as avarice and envy; or through sickness and other calamities. 
 
  A stranger; another than himself.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:3
segments: Be not filled with good--have no burial; live without enjoying life, and come to a disgraceful end.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:4
segments: Name shall be covered with darkness; none shall hear of it.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:5
segments: This; the untimely birth.  For the thought, compare

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:6
segments: Do not all go to one place? that is, since in his long life he has seen no good, what is the profit of living long, as in the end the aged must with all others go to the grave?

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:7
segments:
For his mouth; to satisfy his bodily wants. 
 
  Is not filled; is ever craving more.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:8
segments:
What hath the wise more than the fool? that is, in respect to what has just been named.  In their bodily wants, wise men and fools stand on a level. 
 
  The poor; the poor wise man. 
 
  Knoweth to walk; to walk wisely.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:9
segments:
The sight of the eyes; the sight and enjoyment of present good. 
 
  The wandering of the desire; after absent good.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:10
segments: That which hath been is named already; or, that which is hath been named already.  Compare

. 
 
  Known; from all past experience. 
 
  That it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he; that is, weak, frail, and perishing man, who occupies this world subject to the sovereign appointment of God, and unable to change the course of human affairs which He has established.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:11
segments: What is man the better? literally, "What profit is there to man?" that is, what satisfying good has he?

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 6:12
segments: In this life--what shall be after him; two reasons are given why there is no profit to man: first, no one can show any satisfying good; secondly, no one can understand the future.
